prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses - Loans
prov.text:
The following table provides a rollforward of the allowance for credit losses for each of the periods presented; however, allocation of a portion of the allowance to one segment does not preclude its availability to absorb losses in other segments.

1 The allowance established on acquired PCD loans was recorded through the acquisition-date gross-up of the acquired loans rather than through provision expense and was not material to the Company's total allowance for credit losses.

The allowance for credit losses - loans (“ACL”) was $57.4 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $55.7 million as of December 31, 2025. The ACL as a percentage of total loans was 1.48% at September 30, 2026, compared to 1.49% at December 31, 2025. The ACL as a percentage of nonperforming loans decreased to 91.5% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 95.1% as of December 31, 2025, due primarily to a decrease in the ACL related to franchise finance loans with specific reserves that were charged off during the year.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table shows noninterest expense for each of the periods presented.

Noninterest expense for the third quarter 2026 was $27.3 million, representing an increase of $1.8 million, or 7.1%, compared to $25.5 million for the third quarter 2025. The increase in noninterest expense was due primarily to increases in loan expenses, other noninterest expense, salaries and employee benefits, and marketing, advertising, and promotion expenses. The increase of $0.5 million, or 29.3%, in loan expenses was due primarily to third party servicing and fintech program management fees, as well as collection expense. The increase of $0.4 million, or 21.8%, in other noninterest expense was due primarily to increased risk management costs and expenses associated with OREO. The increase of $0.4 million, or 2.6%, in salaries and employee benefits was due to non-recurring employee severance expense. The increase of $0.3 million, or 52.1%, in marketing, advertising, and promotion expenses was due primarily to increased marketing initiatives during the period.

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $78.4 million, an increase of $7.6 million, or 10.7%, compared to $70.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was due primarily to increases in salaries and employee benefits, loan expenses, and premises and equipment.

net.text: During the third quarter 2026, net income was $4.8 million, or $0.54 diluted earnings per share, compared to a net loss of $41.6 million, or $4.76 diluted loss per share, during the third quarter 2025, representing an increase in net income of $46.4 million and an increase in diluted earnings per share of $5.30. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income was $9.7 million, or $1.10 diluted earnings per share, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025 net loss of $40.5 million, or $4.63 diluted loss per share, resulting in an increase in net income of $50.2 million and an increase in diluted earnings per share of $5.73.

Net interest income.text: The $46.4 million increase in net income for the third quarter 2026 compared to the third quarter 2025 was due primarily to increases of $33.8 million in noninterest income and $4.4 million, or 14.5%, in net interest income, as well as a decrease of $23.2 million, or 66.6%, in the provision for credit losses, partially offset by an increase of $1.8 million, or 7.1%, in noninterest expense and a decrease of $13.2 million in income tax benefit.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income (Loss)
Noninterest income.text:
The following table shows noninterest income (loss) for each of the periods presented.

During the third quarter 2026, noninterest income was $9.2 million, representing an increase of $33.8 million, compared to a loss of $24.6 million for the third quarter 2025. The increase in noninterest income was driven primarily by increases in gain on sale of loans, net loan servicing and service charges and fees, partially offset by a decrease in other noninterest income. The increase of $31.9 million in gain on sale of loans was due primarily to the impact of the aforementioned sale of single tenant lease financing loans, which resulted in a pre-tax loss of $37.8 million. Adjusted for the loan sale, noninterest income totaled $13.2 million for the third quarter 2025. Compared to this adjusted noninterest income, third quarter 2026 noninterest income declined $4.0 million, or 30.2%. The decrease was driven primarily by a decrease of $5.9 million, or 55.3%, in gain on sale of loans due to a decrease in the volume of U.S. Small Business Administration (“SBA”) 7(a) guaranteed loan sales. The increase of $1.1 million, or 157.7%, in net loan servicing was due primarily to the increase in the Company’s loan servicing portfolio following the sale of the single tenant lease financing loans, as well as positive fair value adjustments to the loan servicing asset.

intro.text: When we refer to “First Internet Bancorp,” the “Company,” “we,” “us” and “our” in the remainder of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, we mean First Internet Bancorp and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context indicates otherwise. References to “First Internet Bank” or the “Bank” refer to First Internet Bank of Indiana, an Indiana chartered bank and wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. First Internet Bancorp is a bank holding company headquartered in Fishers, Indiana that conducts its primary business activities through its wholly-owned subsidiary, First Internet Bank of Indiana, an Indiana chartered bank. The Bank was the first state-chartered, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) insured Internet bank and commenced banking operations in 1999. First Internet Bancorp was incorporated under the laws of the State of Indiana on September 15, 2005.
